newsitem.title: USA: NYS gov says Broome County to get 550 jobs.
newsitem.headline: NYS gov says Broome County to get 550 jobs.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Thursday said that Broome County should get 550 new jobs as a result of an international market research and direct mail firm's decision to lease space there.

The company, TeleSpectrum Worldwide, will lease 24,000 square feet of space from International Business Machines at the Glendale Technology Park in Endicott in Broome County, which is located approximately 180 miles west of Albany.
TeleSpectrum, whose yearly payroll for the employees was expected to total about $5.6 million, was projected to spend more than $3 million on equipment and improvements.

The firm, which qualified for wage tax credits, employee tax credits and low-cost power, will get a $250,000 Economic Incentive Payment secured by Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, and Senator Thomas Libous, R-Binghamton, plus $125,000 from Parnership 2000.
"This is another big win for New York State," Pataki said, in prepared remarks.
